Overview/Tax design

Paper 03 · Tax design

The Shape of the Tax

Statutory Incidence, Notches, and the Design of New York City's Mortgage Recording and Transfer Taxes

By Pablo LoschiPublic preprint version 1.0Revised draft in author review

The question

New York's tax schedules put legal charges on mortgage recording and property transfers. How large is the statutory mortgage charge on observed loans, and did sales shift at the buyer-paid transfer-tax thresholds introduced in 2019?

The paper applies the published tax schedule to observed loans and compares transactions at the same nominal price thresholds before and after the reform.

What the evidence says

The schedule-based calculation directly measures the legal charge assigned to financing. The reform comparison documents transaction shifting at new thresholds with enough observations to evaluate. A defined purchase-money carve-out is costed statically, holding transactions fixed; the condominium component uses imputed loans.

These results do not identify who ultimately bears the tax, how transactions would respond to a continuous replacement tax, or an optimal tax rate.

Validation status

The linked Zenodo preprint and separate replication archive are public. A revised submission draft has been prepared locally and is undergoing author review and final legal-source and reference checks. The public DOI currently points to the deposited version 1.0, not that revised draft.
